hero.caption:
Lloyd Lake. This is a front porch standing without a house — all that remains of a Nob Hill house destroyed in the 1906 earthquake. 

It is the only public memorial to the disaster in the City, and is on the lake in Golden Gate Park.
The Neoclassical portal is sited as an architectural folly, a traditional element in the English landscape garden style.

images.filename: Portals of the Past, Golden Gate Park, May 2019.JPG
images.caption: "Portals of the Past" in Golden Gate Park, photographed in May 2019. It is the former doorway of the house of Southern Pacific Railroad executive A. N. Towne, which stood at California and Taylor on Nob Hill. The doorway was the only portion of the house (and much of Nob Hill) to survive the 1906 earthquake and fire; numerous photographs show the doorway standing alone amidst the devastation. Towne's widow donated the doorway to Golden Gate Park in 1909.
